question: Should config.json become a durable MCP capability-policy surface, and should its first version be limited to built-in global and per-account profiles?
rationale: Current code defines runtime gates and baked ceilings but does not determine whether persistent config is an overridable default, a narrowing constraint, or both; that permanent security and compatibility contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Start with built-in profiles
options.body: Approve only built-in global and per-account profiles, resolved after account selection, with explicit CLI override semantics inside baked safety ceilings.

options.title: Approve the full schema
options.body: Adopt custom profiles, per-tool overrides, and account overrides together with a comprehensive validation, precedence, and compatibility contract.

options.title: Keep runtime flags only
options.body: Retain client-specific launch arguments and avoid adding another persistent capability-policy source of truth.

recommendation.title: Start with built-in profiles
recommendation.body: Approve only built-in global and per-account profiles, resolved after account selection, with explicit CLI override semantics inside baked safety ceilings.

likelyOwner.reason: Related capability discussions and the recent config, release, and runtime-safety history make this the best available owner for the permanent product and security contract.
